title: The Tally Thief
brief: Write a mystery set in the Saltglass Reach. Someone has been shaving notches off the council's tally sticks on Cobber's Hold. Harbour Warden Pell Tamsin investigates and names the thief by the end. Play fair with clues.
worldBible: The Saltglass Reach is nine islands joined only by ferries; no bridge can stand because the seabed shifts every spring.
Saltglass forms on the tidal flats after spring tides; a saltglass lamp burns without oil for exactly one night and then goes dark for good.
By Warden law no bell may be rung after sunset; a bell after dark is said to draw the Listeners up from deep water.
Money is tallies: notched driftwood sticks, one notch for one day of labour.
The Warden council meets on Cobber's Hold, the oldest island.
No ferry runs on the night of the dark moon.
Tally sticks are split lengthwise; the council keeps one half and the worker keeps the other, so a shaved half no longer matches its twin.

cast.name: Ilse Varga
traits: missing the two smallest fingers of her right hand

cast.name: Marit Sule
traits: keeps the tally room key on a red cord

mustHold.fact: The islands are joined only by ferries; no bridge can stand between them.
mustHold.violationExample: They walked across the old bridge to Cobber's Hold before dawn.

mustHold.fact: A saltglass lamp burns for exactly one night and then goes dark for good.
mustHold.violationExample: Her saltglass lamp burned for three nights without dimming.

mustHold.fact: By Warden law no bell may be rung after sunset.
mustHold.violationExample: There was no law against ringing bells, so the children rang them all night.

mustHold.fact: The thief is Marit Sule, the council clerk.
mustHold.violationExample: In the end the thief was Doran, who had been shaving notches to pay his debts.

probes.question: Is Pell's blind eye still the right one?
probes.passExample: Pell turned his blind right eye toward the sea, the way he did when he was thinking.
probes.failExample: Pell squinted with his good right eye; the left eye was blind.

probes.question: Is Ilse still missing the two smallest fingers of her right hand?
probes.passExample: Ilse turned the pipe with her three-fingered right hand, the gap where the smallest two had been catching the light.
probes.failExample: Ilse spread all ten fingers on the warm bench.

probes.question: Is Marit named as the thief by the end?
probes.passExample: Marit confessed before the council that she had shaved the notches herself.
